title: Development of a hybrid intervention to promote physical actvitiy related health competence (PAHCO) among nursing professionals
summary: Physical activity is associated with a wide range of positive effects in terms of bio-psycho-social health. Nursing professionals, with almost 30 million members worldwide, are the largest profession in the healthcare sector and have a high level of physical activity due to the nature of their profession. However, the paradox of physical activity applies here, which states that professional-related physical activity does not have the same health benefits as physical activity during leisure time. A high level of professional-related physical activity appears to be associated with a number of adverse health effects. Against this background, promoting physical activity among people with physically demanding jobs should not only focus on increasing the level of physical activity, but also on strengthening the skills required to cope with physical activity in a healthy way. Physical activity-related health literacy plays a crucial role here. The National Action Plan for Health Literacy calls for targeted interventions directly in settings that are particularly important for health promotion measures, including the professional environment. Employees spend an average of just under 55% of their day at work. The workplace therefore has a decisive influence on health and at the same time offers a good starting point for measures to optimize health literacy and physical activity. Ideally, these measures should take individual needs into account, be participatory in nature, and strengthen self-efficacy and perceived control. As part of the BeGeKo-Care project, following a problem analysis, a hybrid intervention to promote the movement-related health literacy of nursing professionals in their professional environment is being developed and scientifically monitored in collaboration with nursing professionals at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf (UKE).

interventions.name: The hybrid intervention consists of two consecutive parts. The first part is carried out digitally and independently by the target group (nursing professionals). The content focuses on increasing movement-related health literacy. The digital part is supplemented by the second part, an exercise group

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Employment at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf as a nurse; German language skills at level B2; informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Employees from other areas; nursing trainees, nursing staff from other clinics (temporary staff); insufficient knowledge of German; no voluntary and independently effective consent
